experiments.title: Dividend month premium — returns are high in the month a dividend is predicted
experiments.hypothesis: Stocks earn positive abnormal returns in months when a dividend is predicted from their own past payment schedule (~53 bps/month vs all other stocks); monthly formation from payments 3/6/9/12 months earlier, long-only predicted payers, post-ex-day reversal measured separately.

literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Stocks earn positive abnormal returns in months when a dividend is predicted from their own past payment schedule (~53 bps/month vs all other stocks); monthly formation from payments 3/6/9/12 months earlier, long-only predicted payers, post-ex-day reversal measured separately.

experiments.title: Intraday periodicity — same half-hour returns repeat at daily lags
experiments.hypothesis: A stock's return in a given half-hour interval positively predicts its return in the same half-hour interval on subsequent days, persisting at least 40 trading days; 13 half-hour intervals, 09:30 ET anchor, completed bars only.

literature_intake.source: Heston, Korajczyk & Sadka, Journal of Finance 65 (2010) 1369-1407
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: A stock's return in a given half-hour interval positively predicts its return in the same half-hour interval on subsequent days, persisting at least 40 trading days; 13 half-hour intervals, 09:30 ET anchor, completed bars only.

experiments.title: R&D intensity — high R&D relative to market value is underpriced
experiments.hypothesis: Among R&D-doing firms, high R&D intensity (R&D scaled by market value of equity) predicts higher subsequent returns, strongest in growth stocks; annual formation from as-filed R&D under EDGAR filed-date discipline.

literature_intake.source: Chan, Lakonishok & Sougiannis, Journal of Finance 56 (2001) 2431-2456 (NBER WP 7223)
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Among R&D-doing firms, high R&D intensity (R&D scaled by market value of equity) predicts higher subsequent returns, strongest in growth stocks; annual formation from as-filed R&D under EDGAR filed-date discipline.

experiments.title: Operating leverage — high operating costs relative to assets earn higher returns
experiments.hypothesis: Firms with high operating leverage (annual operating costs scaled by assets) earn significantly higher average returns; annual formation, intra-industry form ranked within industry, controlling for book-to-market and gross profitability.

literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.

experiments.title: Labor hiring rate — firms hiring slowly earn higher future returns
experiments.hypothesis: Firms with lower labor hiring rates earn higher future stock returns (~7.05%/yr value-weighted low-minus-high hiring+investment spread in the paper); annual formation on employment change, hiring-only sort reported with the investment/asset-growth rate controlled.

literature_intake.source: Bazdresch, Belo & Lin, working paper Sep 2009 (published JFQA 49 (2014) as Belo, Lin & Bazdresch)
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Firms with lower labor hiring rates earn higher future stock returns (~7.05%/yr value-weighted low-minus-high hiring+investment spread in the paper); annual formation on employment change, hiring-only sort reported with the investment/asset-growth rate controlled.

experiments.title: Innovative efficiency — patents per R&D dollar predict returns
experiments.hypothesis: Innovative efficiency (patents granted, or citations, scaled by R&D expenditures with a two-year application-grant lag) is a strong positive predictor of future returns (~38 bps/month value-weighted high-minus-low); annual formation, 12-month hold, R&D-doing firms only, R&D intensity controlled.

literature_intake.source: Hirshleifer, Hsu & Li, Journal of Financial Economics 107 (2013) 632-654
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Innovative efficiency (patents granted, or citations, scaled by R&D expenditures with a two-year application-grant lag) is a strong positive predictor of future returns (~38 bps/month value-weighted high-minus-low); annual formation, 12-month hold, R&D-doing firms only, R&D intensity controlled.

experiments.title: Option-implied volatility skew (smirk) — steep smirks predict low returns
experiments.hypothesis: Stocks with a steep volatility smirk (IV of out-of-the-money puts minus at-the-money calls, monthly formation, 30-91 days to maturity) earn lower subsequent returns over 1-week to 3-month holds.

literature_intake.source: Xing, Zhang & Zhao, JFQA 45 (2010); comparison: Fu, Arisoy, Shackleton & Umutlu, Liverpool repository paper
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
